content:
incident-bot: PAGE (P1) - High GPU queue length and elevated 429s observed for hosted inference cluster 'eu-west-1-gpupool'. Auto-scale failing to add nodes. alert_id=INC-1932104567

emma: paging in — saw the bot. 429 spike started ~5m ago, queue depth climbing to ~26k reqs.

raj: digging into autoscaler logs now. last scale event was 12m ago and it hit max_nodes.

olivia: customer-facing channels reporting user-facing 429s for batching endpoints. SE flagged 3 paying customers seeing errors.

ben: confirming metrics: GPU utilization at 99%, queue_processing_rate flat, incoming RPS jumped 3x on a couple of routes. Token bucket counters show drop to zero on multiple tiers.

emma: suspected cause: rate cap + tier config too tight under burst plus autoscaler max cap reached. Is there any recent deploy?

oncall-pager: @emma you're oncall. please coordinate mitigations and post customer impact summary.

raj: not a recent deploy. autoscale policy was unchanged. Looks like scale happened but hit `max_nodes: 40` and further scale suppressed by cooldown window. Cooldown remaining ~6m.

olivia: impacted customers: acme-inc (enterprise), quickchat (startup-paid), internal-sandbox. Severity: acme-inc traffic 200 requests/min failing intermittently.

ben: workaround options: 1) relax token bucket refill rates for non-enterprise tiers, 2) temporarily raise autoscale max_nodes, 3) route high-throughput customers to dedicated pool (if available), 4) degrade to smaller model variant to free GPU slots.

emma: prioritize quickest: increase autoscale cap + adjust token bucket for bursty tiers. Raj can you request emergency scale increase?

raj: filing infra change now — request to bump max_nodes to 60 for eu-west-1-gpupool. ETA on nodes joining ~4-7m depending on image pull. Filed CHG-1932 with infra.

olivia: I'll notify affected customers that we're working on capacity and may see intermittent 429s for ~10m. cc @ben for confirmation once throttles eased.

ben: starting live tuning: lowering conservative rate limits on these tiers. Current policy snippet:

```
# rate tier config (yaml)
tiers:
  default:
    token_rate: 50/s
    bucket_size: 100
  startup-paid:
    token_rate: 200/s
    bucket_size: 400
  enterprise:
    token_rate: 1000/s
    bucket_size: 2000
```

ben: changing `default.token_rate` -> 150/s and `default.bucket_size` -> 500 to allow more short-term concurrency. Applying patch to config canary on one region first.

emma: apply to eu-west-1 canary only. avoid global blast.

ben: applied canary patch to eu-west-1. Pushed config and reloaded rate-limiter service. Observing metrics...

ops-bot: CONFIG-RELOAD successful for rate-limiter-eu-west-1 at 1932105701.

ben: initial signs: 429 rate dropping from 18% -> 9% in canary nodes. queue length stabilizing where patch applied.

raj: infra update: nodes provisioning, expected join within 3m. cooldown still in effect but manual override approved for emergency.

olivia: customer update sent to acme-inc and quickchat. they acknowledged and are monitoring.

emma: decision tree: if canary improvements propagate and new nodes join, we'll keep new autoscale cap and leave token changes for 30m then revert to original defaults with a gradual ramp. If not, route enterprise customers to dedicated fallback.

ben: also found misapplied per-route override for `/v1/stream` that had `burst=false` set accidentally. Fixing now — that was forcing small bucket sizes.

ben: patched per-route override removed, reloaded. ops-bot shows config flush.

ops-bot: CONFIG-FLUSH complete for route-overrides at 1932106444.

emma: what's the ETA to normal for SLAs?

raj: nodes are joining right now, first of 8 new GPUs became ready. autoscaler cap increased to 60 and join rate good. expect queue drain in ~6m.

ben: 429 rate in eu-west-1 down to 3.6% overall. canary zones at ~1%. Good signal.

olivia: customers reported errors mostly cleared. acme-inc says traffic normalizing but will keep support case open for 1h.

emma: great. write down mitigation steps and follow-up actions for postmortem. who will own the write-up?

raj: I'll own infra action items (autoscale cooldown logic, emergency override docs).

ben: I'll own rate-limit config follow-up: audit per-route overrides, and add a safety that prevents `burst=false` on high-throughput routes without review.

olivia: I'll own customer comms and impact timeline.

emma: incident status -> mitigated. moving to monitoring and post-incident review. Please add links to graphs and logs in the doc.

oncall-pager: incident resolved, paging closed. Reminder: create postmortem within 48h. :white_check_mark:

ben: quick notes to include in postmortem: root causes: (1) autoscaler hit configured max_nodes under large burst, (2) cooldown prevented timely rescale, (3) per-route rate override inadvertently small & global default too conservative. Mitigations implemented: emergency scale increase, token bucket refill increase for default tier canary, removed bad per-route override, will add safeties and change autoscale policy to allow one-time emergency burst overcommit for XX minutes.

emma: thanks all. dropping support Slack channel link and incident page here: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1932104567

olivia: adding note: postmortem should include timeline of customer-facing errors and planned SLA credits if threshold breached.

ben: logs snippet (trimmed):
```
[1932105601] rate_limiter: bucket_default=0 tokens=0 incoming=350/s granted=12/s -> 429
[1932105680] rate_limiter: applied override route=/v1/stream burst=false -> bucket_size=10
[1932105765] autoscaler: reached max_nodes=40, cooldown=300s remaining=360s
[1932105900] config: canary rate change applied default.token_rate=150/s
[1932106022] node-manager: new-node-1 ready
```

emma: final: let's meet for postmortem tomorrow 10am. I'll send calendar. Good job on fast remediation. :clap:

oncall-pager: thread closed at 1932108420.
